title: Completion at a quasi-finite prime is a direct factor of the completed base change
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map where $R$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, and assume that $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (Stacks Algebra Definition 00PL). Let $R_{\mathfrak p}$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ be the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^nR_{\mathfrak p}$, $(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge=\varprojlim_nS_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q^nS_{\mathfrak q}$ their completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let $\phi:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ be the natural ring map $x\otimes y\mapsto\hat\varphi(x)\cdot\iota(y)$, where $\hat\varphi:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is induced by the local homomorphism $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\iota:S\to S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is the canonical map. Then there are a ring $B$ and a ring map $\beta:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to B$ such that $(\phi,\beta):(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS\cong(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ as $S$-algebras and as $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebras, with $B$ an $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra via $\beta$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime) and its proof, including the final 'sanity check' that the projection to $S_{\mathfrak q}^\wedge$ is the natural map (uses Lemma Tag 00QB lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure and Lemma Tag 07N9 lemma-completion-finite-extension); cited in More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07PP

proof.text: *A finite subalgebra agreeing with $S$ away from $g$.* Since $S$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra and $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-finite-subalgebra-away] gives an $R$-subalgebra $S'\subseteq S$, with inclusion $i:S'\to S$, which is a finitely generated $R$-module, and $g\in S'$, $g\notin\mathfrak q$, such that $i_g:S'_g\to S_g$, $y/g^n\mapsto i(y)/g^n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], is an isomorphism. Put $\mathfrak q'=i^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=S'\cap\mathfrak q$, a prime ideal of $S'$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q'$; its inverse image in $R$ is $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$, since $R\to S$ factors as $R\to S'\xrightarrow{i}S$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'There exists a finite $R$-algebra $S'\subset S$ and an element $g\in S'$, $g\notin\mathfrak q'=S'\cap\mathfrak q$ such that $S'_g=S_g$', by Lemma Tag 00QB (lemma-quasi-finite-open-integral-closure, line 30906) with Theorem Tag 00Q9

proof.text:
*$S'_{\mathfrak q'}\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$ and on completions.* The map $i_{\mathfrak q'}:S'_{\mathfrak q'}	o S_{\mathfrak q}$, $y/t\mapsto i(y)/i(t)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] (well defined since $t
otin\mathfrak q'$ means $i(t)
otin\mathfrak q$) is an isomorphism. Surjective: for $s\in S$, surjectivity of $i_g$ gives $y\in S'$, $k\ge0$ with $s/1=y/g^k$ in $S_g$, i.e. $g^l(g^ks-y)=0$ in $S$ for some $l$, so $g^Ns\in S'$ for $N=k+l$; given $s/t\in S_{\mathfrak q}$ choose $N$ with $g^Ns,g^Nt\in S'$; then $g^Nt
otin\mathfrak q'$ and $s/t=i_{\mathfrak q'}(g^Ns/g^Nt)$. Injective: if $i(y)/1=0$ in $S_{\mathfrak q}$, then $ty=0$ in $S$ for some $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$; as above $u=g^Nt\in S'$ for some $N$, $u
otin\mathfrak q'$ (as $g,t
otin\mathfrak q$), and $uy=g^N(ty)=0$, so $y/1=0$ in $S'_{\mathfrak q'}$; a general element $y/t$ is $(y/1)(t/1)^{-1}$. An isomorphism of local rings carries the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q'S'_{\mathfrak q'}$ onto $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ and its powers onto the powers, so it induces isomorphisms $S'_{\mathfrak q'}/(\mathfrak q'S'_{\mathfrak q'})^n\cong S_{\mathfrak q}/(\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q})^n$ compatible with the transition maps, hence a ring isomorphism of completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $\alpha:(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge	o(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$. Let $\psi:(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge	o(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$ be induced by the local map $R_{\mathfrak p}	o S'_{\mathfrak q'}$ and $\iota':S'	o(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$ the canonical map. Since $R_{\mathfrak p}	o S'_{\mathfrak q'}\xrightarrow{i_{\mathfrak q'}}S_{\mathfrak q}$ is the map $R_{\mathfrak p}	o S_{\mathfrak q}$ and $S'	o S'_{\mathfrak q'}	o S_{\mathfrak q}$ is $S'\xrightarrow{i}S	o S_{\mathfrak q}$, comparing level by level gives $\alpha\circ\psi=\hat\varphi$ and $\alpha\circ\iota'=\iota\circ i$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'in particular $S'_{\mathfrak q'}=S_{\mathfrak q}$' and 'the isomorphism $S'_{\mathfrak q'}=S_\mathfrak q$ determines an isomorphism on completions' (both written out here)

proof.text: *The completed base change of the finite algebra $S'$.* Let $T=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS'$. $R$ is Noetherian and $S'$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; let $\mathfrak q'_1=\mathfrak q',\mathfrak q'_2,\dots,\mathfrak q'_m$ be the primes of $S'$ over $\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak q'$ is one by step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] the ring map $T\to\prod_{i=1}^m(S'_{\mathfrak q'_i})^\wedge$ whose $i$-th component is $x\otimes y\mapsto\psi_i(x)\iota'_i(y)$ ($\psi_i$, $\iota'_i$ the maps induced by $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S'_{\mathfrak q'_i}$ and $S'\to S'_{\mathfrak q'_i}$) is an isomorphism (it is compatible with the $S'$- and $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra structures). Its first component is $\phi':T\to(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\psi(x)\iota'(y)$. Let $e\in T$ be the element mapping to $(1,0,\dots,0)$: $e$ is idempotent, $\phi'(e)=1$, $\phi'(1-e)=0$, and the restriction of $\phi'$ to the ring $Te$ (with unit $e$) is a ring isomorphism $\phi'_e:Te\to(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$, because the isomorphism carries $Te$ onto $(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge\times0\times\dots\times0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): '$R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS'=(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge\times B'$ by Lemma Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension, line 23135)'

proof.text: *Comparison with $U=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS$.* Let $U=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge\otimes_RS$ and $j=1\otimes i:T\to U$, a ring map. Then $\phi\circ j=\alpha\circ\phi'$: both are ring maps, hence additive, and on a generator $x\otimes y$ ($x\in(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$, $y\in S'$) they give $\hat\varphi(x)\iota(i(y))=\alpha(\psi(x))\alpha(\iota'(y))$ by step 2.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): the 'sanity check' that the induced map to $S_\mathfrak q^\wedge$ is the natural one (for $x\otimes1$ 'the natural map $R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\to S_\mathfrak q^\wedge$ factors through $(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$'); here it is checked on the image of $T$, which by steps 5-7 suffices

proof.text: *$T$ and $U$ agree after inverting $g$.* Regard $T$ and $U$ as $S'$-modules via $y\mapsto1\otimes y$ and $y\mapsto1\otimes i(y)$; $j$ is $S'$-linear. Write $N=(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$ (an $R$-module) and use the symmetry $N\otimes_RM\cong M\otimes_RN$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with $A=S'$, the multiplicative set of powers of $g$, and $M=S'$, resp. $M=S$ viewed as an $S'$-module via $i$, whose localization at $g$ is $S_g$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]), $\ell':T\to N\otimes_RS'_g$ and $\ell:U\to N\otimes_RS_g$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y/1$, are localizations at $g$, i.e. induce isomorphisms $T_g\cong N\otimes_RS'_g$ and $U_g\cong N\otimes_RS_g$, $(x\otimes y)/g^k\mapsto x\otimes(y/g^k)$. Under them the map $j_g:T_g\to U_g$, $t/g^k\mapsto j(t)/g^k$, becomes $1\otimes i_g$ (check on the generators $(x\otimes y)/g^k$), which is an isomorphism with inverse $1\otimes i_g^{-1}$ since $i_g$ is one (step 1). Hence $j_g$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'Since $S'_g=S_g$ we also have $(R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS')_g=(R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS)_g$'

proof.text: *$g$ is a unit on the first factor.* Write $\gamma=1\otimes g\in T$; then $j(\gamma)=1\otimes i(g)$, which is the element by which $g$ acts on $U$. $\phi'(\gamma)=\iota'(g)$ is the image of $g/1$, a unit of $S'_{\mathfrak q'}$ because $g\notin\mathfrak q'$, hence a unit of $(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$. Since $\phi'_e$ is a ring isomorphism (step 3) and $\phi'_e(\gamma e)=\phi'(\gamma)$, $\gamma e$ is a unit of $Te$: there is $v\in T$ with $v\gamma e=e$. Let $f=j(e)\in U$, an idempotent, and $w=j(v)$; then $w\,j(\gamma)\,f=f$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'under this product decomposition $g$ maps to a pair $(u,b')$ with $u\in(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge$ a unit because $g\notin\mathfrak q'$'

proof.text: *$j$ maps $Te$ isomorphically onto $Uf$.* $j$ restricts to a ring map $j_e:Te\to Uf$ (units $e\mapsto f$). Surjective: for $u\in U$, step 5 gives $t\in T$ and $k\ge0$ with $u/1=j(t)/g^k$ in $U_g$, i.e. $j(\gamma)^l(j(\gamma)^ku-j(t))=0$ for some $l$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; multiplying by $f$ and by $w^{k+l}$ and using $w\,j(\gamma)f=f$ gives $uf=w^{k+l}j(\gamma)^lj(t)f=j(v^{k+l}\gamma^lte)$. Injective: if $j(te)=0$, then $j_g(te/1)=0$, so $te/1=0$ in $T_g$ by step 5, i.e. $\gamma^lte=0$ for some $l$; multiplying by $v^l$ and using $v\gamma e=e$ gives $te=0$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'since $g\mapsto(u,b')$ where $u$ is a unit we see that $(S'_{\mathfrak q'})^\wedge=A$', with $A=(R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS)f$ the factor induced by the product decomposition of $R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS'$

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Put $B=U(1-f)$, a ring with unit $1-f$, and $\beta:U\to B$, $u\mapsto u(1-f)$, a ring map. Since $\phi(1-f)=\phi(j(1-e))=\alpha(\phi'(1-e))=0$ (step 4), $\phi(u)=\phi(uf)$ for all $u$, and the restriction $\phi_f:Uf\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is a ring map with $\phi_f\circ j_e=\alpha\circ\phi'_e$ (step 4); as $j_e$, $\alpha$, $\phi'_e$ are isomorphisms (steps 7, 2, 3), so is $\phi_f$. The map $U\to Uf\times U(1-f)$, $u\mapsto(uf,u(1-f))$, is a ring isomorphism (inverse $(a,b)\mapsto a+b$, as $f$ is idempotent), and $(\phi,\beta)$ is its composite with $\phi_f\times\mathrm{id}_B$; hence $(\phi,\beta):U\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ is a ring isomorphism. In particular, giving $(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge\times B$ the $S$-algebra structure $y\mapsto(\iota(y),\beta(1\otimes y))$ and the $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebra structure $x\mapsto(\hat\varphi(x),\beta(x\otimes1))$, it is an isomorphism of $S$-algebras and of $(R_{\mathfrak p})^\wedge$-algebras, since $\phi(1\otimes y)=\iota(y)$ and $\phi(x\otimes1)=\hat\varphi(x)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064): 'The product decomposition for $R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS'$ induces a product decomposition $R_\mathfrak p^\wedge\otimes_RS=A\times B$ ... this also tells us that $A=S_\mathfrak q^\wedge$', and the final sanity check (here the projection is shown to be the natural map $\phi$ by step 4 instead of the computation with $g^ny$)

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NC (lemma-completion-at-quasi-finite-prime, line 31064) and its proof; uses Theorem Tag 00Q9 / Lemma Tag 00QB and Lemma Tag 07N9. The final sanity check is reorganized: the natural map is compared with the decomposition on the image of $T$ (step 4) rather than on elements $g^ny$.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks 07NC and its proof (algebra.tex:31064), 00QB, 00Q9 and 07N9. Statement kept; its citation of quasi-finiteness repointed from [pqf-def-quasifinite] (scheme definition) to the affine definition node [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (stmt_deps changed accordingly). Stacks cites 00QB, which assumes S quasi-finite at every prime; the pointwise form needed (00Q9 plus the finite-subalgebra construction of the proof of 00QB(3), 'details omitted') is the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-finite-subalgebra-away (Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.exists_fg_and_exists_notMem_and_awayMap_bijective). Proof in 8 steps: finite subalgebra S' and g; S'_{q'}=S_q written out (Stacks 'in particular') and the induced iso on completions; 07N9 for S' via [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension]; comparison phi o j = alpha o phi'; T_g = U_g via [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base]; g a unit on the first factor; Te = Uf; conclusion with B = U(1-f). Stacks' sanity check (that the projection is the natural map) is carried by step 4 and the construction: phi itself is shown to restrict to an isomorphism on Uf and to vanish on 1-f, so the computation with g^n y is not needed. The 'in particular' clause (S- and (R_p)^-algebra structures) is the last part of step 8, as used by the citer lem-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-quasi-finite-ascent.

reviewed.note: 8 steps following Stacks 07NC (with the pointwise form of Zariski's main theorem as a new unsplit node, since 00QB assumes quasi-finiteness everywhere): S' finite with S'_g = S_g; S'_{q'} = S_q written out; 07N9 for S' with the idempotent e of the first factor; phi j = alpha phi'; T_g = U_g; g a unit on Te; j: Te = Uf; conclusion with B = U(1-f). Statement citation repointed to def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime.

lean.statement: theorem completion_at_quasiFiniteAtPrime (R : Type u) (S : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] [Algebra.FiniteType R S] [IsNoetherianRing R] (q : PrimeSpectrum S) (hq : IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime R S q) : let p : Ideal R := q.comap (algebraMap R S) let Rp := Localization.AtPrime p let Sq := Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal let Ip := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Rp let Iq := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal Sq let Rph := AdicCompletion Ip Rp let Sqh := AdicCompletion Iq Sq let f : Rp →+* Sq := Localization.localRingHom p q.asIdeal (algebraMap R S) rfl let U := TensorProduct R Rph S ∃ ψ : Rph →+* Sqh, (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : Rph) (a : Rp), AdicCompletion.evalₐ Ip n x = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ip ^ n) a → AdicCompletion.evalₐ Iq n (ψ x) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (Iq ^ n) (f a)) ∧ ∃ (B : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing B) (β : U →+* B) (φ : U →+* Sqh), (∀ (x : Rph) (y : S), φ (TensorProduct.tmul R x y) = ψ x * algebraMap Sq Sqh (algebraMap S Sq y)) ∧ ∃ e : U ≃+* Sqh × B, e.toRingHom = RingHom.prod φ β

reviewed_lean.note: R->S CommRing+Algebra; R Noetherian (IsNoetherianRing); S finite type (Algebra.FiniteType); q prime (PrimeSpectrum); p = comap; quasi-finite at q = recorded Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime; Rp,Sq = Localization.AtPrime; completions AdicCompletion at maximalIdeal; local map = Localization.localRingHom (F1 72b404dc7 form); psi fixed level-by-level; phi pinned on pure tensors x⊗y ↦ psi x * iota y; B, beta existential in max u v; e : U ≃+* Sqh × B with e = prod phi beta encodes S- and Rph-algebra iso
